records.source: Καὶ εἶδον ἄλλον ἄγγελον ἰσχυρὸν καταβαίνοντα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, περιβεβλημένον νεφέλην, καὶ ἡ ἶρις ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος, καὶ οἱ πόδες αὐτοῦ ὡς στῦλοι πυρός, καὶ ἔχων ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ βιβλαρίδιον ἠνεῳγμένον.
records.gloss: And I saw another angel mighty coming down out of the heaven, having been clothed with a cloud, and the rainbow on the head of him, and the face of him as the sun, and the feet of him as pillars of fire, \v 2 and having in the hand of him a little scroll having been opened.
pieces: Then another mighty angel came into view, coming down from heaven. A cloud was his clothing, and the rainbow crowned his head; his face shone like the sun, his legs were like pillars of fire,
and he held a small scroll, open, in his hand.

L.1: And I saw another mighty angel coming down from heaven, clothed with a cloud, and the rainbow [was] over his head, and his face [was] like the sun, and his feet like pillars of fire,
L.2: and he had in his hand a little scroll, opened.

R.1: Then I saw another powerful angel coming down from heaven. He was dressed in a cloud. There was a rainbow over his head. His face was as bright as the sun. His legs were like tall columns of fire.
R.2: He was holding a small scroll in his hand. It was open.

decisions.choice: a mighty angel who bears the marks of God's glory
decisions.reason: The cloud, the rainbow, the face like the sun and the fiery legs recall the throne of 4:3 and the risen Christ of 1:15-16, and some take the figure to be Christ. But John calls him "another angel", like the strong angel of 5:2, and in 10:6 he swears by God. He is most likely an angel who carries God's glory as his messenger.

decisions.choice: a little scroll, lying open
alternatives: the same scroll as in chapter 5, now opened
a different, smaller message for John to proclaim
decisions.reason: βιβλαρίδιον is a diminutive, "a little scroll". It is open, unlike the sealed scroll of 5:1, and John is to eat it and prophesy (10:9-11). Whether it is the scroll of chapter 5, now unsealed, or a separate message is not settled.

decisions.choice: feet (L); legs (B, R)
decisions.reason: πόδες can include the leg, and "pillars" fits legs better than feet.

records.heading: The angel and the little scroll

records.source: καὶ ἔθηκεν τὸν πόδα αὐτοῦ τὸν δεξιὸν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης, τὸν δὲ εὐώνυμον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἔκραξεν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ὥσπερ λέων μυκᾶται.
records.gloss: And he placed the foot of him the right on the sea, and the left on the land, \v 3 and he cried out with voice loud as a lion roars.
pieces: Planting his right foot on the sea and his left on the land,
he called out in a great voice, as a lion roars.

L.2: And he placed his right foot on the sea and the left on the land,
L.3: and he cried out with a loud voice, as a lion roars.

R.2: He put his right foot on the sea and his left foot on the land.
R.3: He shouted loudly, and it sounded like a lion roaring.

decisions.choice: one foot on the sea, one on the land: a message for the whole earth
decisions.reason: Standing over sea and land, the angel claims the whole world. What he announces concerns all of it (10:6, 11).

decisions.choice: a lion's roar: the voice of the LORD in the prophets
decisions.reason: "The lion has roared; who will not fear? The Lord GOD has spoken; who can but prophesy?" (Amos 3:8; compare Hosea 11:10; Joel 3:16).

records.source: καὶ ὅτε ἔκραξεν, ἐλάλησαν αἱ ἑπτὰ βρονταὶ τὰς ἑαυτῶν φωνάς.
records.gloss: And when he cried out, spoke the seven thunders the of themselves voices.
pieces: When he had called out, the seven thunders spoke with their voices.

L.3: And when he cried out, the seven thunders spoke with their own voices.

R.3: When he shouted, the seven thunders answered. They spoke with voices of their own.

decisions.choice: seven thunders: the voice of the LORD in Psalm 29
decisions.reason: Psalm 29 describes the thunder as "the voice of the LORD" seven times. The article, "the seven thunders", suggests something known, and their words are a message from God.

records.source: καὶ ὅτε ἐλάλησαν αἱ ἑπτὰ βρονταί, ἤμελλον γράφειν· καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ λέγουσαν· Σφράγισον ἃ ἐλάλησαν αἱ ἑπτὰ βρονταί, καὶ μὴ αὐτὰ γράψῃς.
records.gloss: And when spoke the seven thunders, I was about to write; and I heard a voice out of the heaven saying: Seal what spoke the seven thunders, and not them write.
pieces: As soon as the seven thunders had spoken, I was ready to write, but a voice from heaven told me, "Seal up the words of the seven thunders; do not write them down."

L.4: And when the seven thunders had spoken, I was about to write, and I heard a voice from heaven saying, "Seal up what the seven thunders have spoken, and do not write it down."

R.4: When the seven thunders had spoken, I was ready to write down what they said. But I heard a voice from heaven. It said, "Keep secret what the seven thunders said. Do not write it down."

decisions.choice: seal up: keep it hidden
decisions.reason: To seal what was spoken means to keep it secret, as Daniel was told to seal up the words until the time of the end (Daniel 12:4, 9). Not everything John heard is to be made known (compare 2 Corinthians 12:4). At the end of the book he is told the opposite about his prophecy: "Do not seal up the words" (22:10).

decisions.choice: seal up (L, B); keep secret (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what sealing means here (m1).

records.source: καὶ ὁ ἄγγελος, ὃν εἶδον ἑστῶτα ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ἦρεν τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ τὴν δεξιὰν εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, καὶ ὤμοσεν τῷ ζῶντι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, ὃς ἔκτισεν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ, ὅτι χρόνος οὐκέτι ἔσται·
records.gloss: And the angel whom I saw standing on the sea and on the land lifted the hand of him the right to the heaven \v 6 and swore by the [one] living into the ages of the ages, who created the heaven and the things in it and the earth and the things in it and the sea and the things in it, that time no longer will be,
pieces: The angel I had seen standing on sea and land lifted his right hand toward heaven

and took an oath by the one who lives forever and ever, the maker of heaven and everything in it, of the earth and everything in it, and of the sea and everything in it, that there would be no more delay.

L.5: And the angel whom I saw standing on the sea and on the land raised his right hand to heaven
L.6: and swore by the one who lives for the ages of the ages, who created heaven and what is in it, and the earth and what is in it, and the sea and what is in it, that there will be no more delay.

R.5: Then the angel I saw standing on the sea and on the land raised his right hand toward heaven.
R.6: He made a promise in the name of God, who lives forever and ever. God made the sky and everything in it, the earth and everything in it, and the sea and everything in it. The angel promised that there would be no more waiting.

decisions.choice: raising the hand and swearing: Daniel 12:7
decisions.reason: In Daniel 12:7 the man clothed in linen raises his hands to heaven and swears by the one who lives forever that the end will come after "a time, times and half a time". Here the angel swears that there will be no more delay.

decisions.choice: no more delay: the time of waiting is over
decisions.reason: χρόνος usually means time, and older translations read "there should be time no longer". Here, with "but in the days of the seventh angel" following, it means that God will wait no longer. It answers the martyrs' question, "How long?", and the reply that they must wait "a little while" (6:10-11).

decisions.choice: the Creator of heaven, earth and sea
decisions.reason: The oath is made by God as Creator of all three realms, as in Exodus 20:11 and Nehemiah 9:6. The angel stands on two of them and raises his hand to the third.

decisions.choice: God (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names God, of whom the title is used (4:9-10).

records.source: ἀλλ’ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῆς φωνῆς τοῦ ἑβδόμου ἀγγέλου, ὅταν μέλλῃ σαλπίζειν, καὶ ἐτελέσθη τὸ μυστήριον τοῦ θεοῦ, ὡς εὐηγγέλισεν τοὺς ἑαυτοῦ δούλους τοὺς προφήτας.
records.gloss: but in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he is about to blow trumpet, also was completed the mystery of the God, as he announced to the of himself slaves the prophets.
pieces: Instead, when the days come for the seventh angel's trumpet, when he is about to blow it, God's mystery will reach its completion, the good news {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} announced to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants the prophets.

L.7: But in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he is about to blow his trumpet, the mystery of God will be completed, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} announced [it] to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} slaves the prophets.

R.7: When the seventh angel is ready to blow his trumpet, God's mystery will be finished. This mystery is God's secret plan. He told it as good news to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants, the prophets.

decisions.choice: the mystery of God: his hidden purpose, now carried through to the end
decisions.reason: A mystery in the New Testament is God's plan, hidden before and now made known (Romans 16:25-26; Ephesians 3:3-9). Its completion is the coming of God's kingdom, announced when the seventh trumpet sounds (11:15).

decisions.choice: was completed: a past tense for something sure to happen
decisions.reason: ἐτελέσθη is a past tense used of the future: when the trumpet sounds, the mystery will be as good as finished.

decisions.choice: announced to his slaves the prophets: Amos 3:7
decisions.reason: "The Lord GOD does nothing without revealing his secret to his servants the prophets" (Amos 3:7). εὐηγγέλισεν is the verb of preaching good news: God's purpose is good news, even when it includes judgment.

decisions.choice: mystery (L, B); mystery ... God's secret plan (R)
decisions.reason: Mystery is a key term, kept at every level. Readable explains it.

decisions.choice: announced (L); the good news he announced (B); told it as good news (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out that the verb means to announce good news (m3).

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it (1:1); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: Καὶ ἡ φωνὴ ἣν ἤκουσα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, πάλιν λαλοῦσαν μετ’ ἐμοῦ καὶ λέγουσαν· Ὕπαγε λάβε τὸ βιβλίον τὸ ἠνεῳγμένον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ τοῦ ἀγγέλου τοῦ ἑστῶτος ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
records.gloss: And the voice which I heard out of the heaven, again speaking with me and saying: Go, take the scroll the having been opened in the hand of the angel the standing on the sea and on the land.
pieces: The voice from heaven that I had heard spoke with me once again. "Go," it said, "and take the scroll lying open in the hand of the angel who stands on sea and land."

L.8: And the voice that I had heard from heaven [was] again speaking with me and saying, "Go, take the scroll that is open in the hand of the angel who stands on the sea and on the land."

R.8: Then the voice from heaven spoke to me again. It said, "Go and take the open scroll from the hand of the angel. He is the one standing on the sea and on the land."

decisions.choice: a sentence without a main verb
decisions.reason: The Greek begins with "the voice" and continues with participles, "speaking" and "saying", without a main verb. The sense is plain: the voice spoke again.

decisions.choice: the scroll: the little scroll of 10:2
decisions.reason: βιβλίον is the ordinary word for scroll, but it refers to the little scroll already described.

records.source: καὶ ἀπῆλθα πρὸς τὸν ἄγγελον λέγων αὐτῷ δοῦναί μοι τὸ βιβλαρίδιον.
records.gloss: And I went to the angel, telling him to give me the little scroll.
pieces: I went over to the angel and told him to hand me the little scroll.

L.9: And I went to the angel, telling him to give me the little scroll.

R.9: So I went to the angel and asked him for the small scroll.

decisions.choice: telling him to give: a request
decisions.reason: The infinitive after "telling" reports what John asked for.

records.source: καὶ λέγει μοι· Λάβε καὶ κατάφαγε αὐτό, καὶ πικρανεῖ σου τὴν κοιλίαν, ἀλλ’ ἐν τῷ στόματί σου ἔσται γλυκὺ ὡς μέλι.
records.gloss: And he says to me: Take and eat up it, and it will make bitter your stomach, but in the mouth of you it will be sweet as honey.
pieces: "Take it," he told me, "and eat it up. It will make your stomach bitter, though in your mouth it will be sweet as honey."

L.9: And he says to me, "Take and eat it, and it will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be sweet as honey."

R.9: He said, "Take it and eat it. It will make your stomach feel bitter and sick. But in your mouth it will taste as sweet as honey."

decisions.choice: eating the scroll: Ezekiel's call
decisions.reason: Ezekiel was told to eat a scroll written with words of lament and woe, and it was sweet as honey in his mouth (Ezekiel 2:8-3:3; compare Jeremiah 15:16). To eat the scroll is to take God's message in fully before speaking it.

decisions.choice: sweet and bitter: God's word is good, and its message brings grief
decisions.reason: God's word is sweet (Psalm 19:11; 119:103), but the message John must now speak includes judgment and the suffering of God's people (chapter 11), and taking it in is bitter.

records.source: καὶ ἔλαβον τὸ βιβλαρίδιον ἐκ τῆς χειρὸς τοῦ ἀγγέλου καὶ κατέφαγον αὐτό, καὶ ἦν ἐν τῷ στόματί μου ὡς μέλι γλυκύ· καὶ ὅτε ἔφαγον αὐτό, ἐπικράνθη ἡ κοιλία μου.
records.gloss: And I took the little scroll out of the hand of the angel and ate up it, and it was in the mouth of me as honey sweet; and when I ate it, was made bitter the stomach of me.
pieces: I took the little scroll out of the angel's hand and ate it up. It was as sweet as honey in my mouth, but when I had eaten it my stomach became bitter.

L.10: And I took the little scroll from the hand of the angel and ate it, and it was sweet as honey in my mouth, and when I had eaten it, my stomach was made bitter.

R.10: I took the small scroll from the angel's hand and ate it. It tasted as sweet as honey. But after I ate it, my stomach felt bitter and sick.

decisions.choice: it happened as he was told
decisions.reason: John's action repeats the angel's words, with the order of sweet and bitter as he experienced them: first the taste, then the bitterness.

records.source: Καὶ λέγουσίν μοι· Δεῖ σε πάλιν προφητεῦσαι ἐπὶ λαοῖς καὶ ἔθνεσιν καὶ γλώσσαις καὶ βασιλεῦσιν πολλοῖς.
records.gloss: And they say to me: It is necessary you again to prophesy about peoples and nations and tongues and kings many.
pieces: Then they said to me, "Once more you must prophesy, concerning many peoples and nations and languages and kings."

L.11: And they say to me, "You must prophesy again about many peoples and nations and languages and kings."

R.11: Then I was told, "You must speak God's message again. You must tell it about many peoples, nations, languages, and kings."

decisions.choice: they say: I was told
decisions.reason: The plural with no subject is a way of saying that someone spoke without naming who.

decisions.choice: about, or against, many peoples
decisions.reason: ἐπὶ can mean "about", "to" or "against". The prophecy concerns the nations and their kings, and much of it is judgment. Jeremiah was appointed "over nations and over kingdoms" (Jeremiah 1:10).

decisions.choice: kings in place of tribes
decisions.reason: The familiar list, "peoples, nations, languages, tribes" (5:9; 7:9), here ends with "many kings": the prophecy that follows deals with rulers and powers (chapters 13 and 17).

decisions.choice: prophesy (L, B); speak God's message (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what it means to prophesy.
